title: Wire the SDD workflow
intro: Don't recite the workflow — build it. One wire is forbidden, and it has a name.
briefing: Route a stakeholder's intent all the way to merged code. Every stage must be wired in its proper order — and the inspector rejects any blueprint where intent reaches implementation directly. That wire is called vibe coding.

rules.label: Intent lands in the constitution first
Each roadmap phase gets a feature spec
The agent implements from the committed spec
Validation reviews the result against the spec
No vibe coding: intent never goes straight to implementation

debrief: The chain you wired — intent → constitution → feature spec → implement → validate → merge — is the whole methodology in one picture. The forbidden wire is the definition of vibe coding: intent jumping straight to implementation, leaving nothing captured in between. Notice what each captured stage buys you: the constitution makes intent durable and shared, the feature spec makes it precise and reviewable, and validation closes the loop by checking the build against the words — not against your memory of a chat.
